pageCache.text:
At King's Academy Rowner we work successfully together to achieve excellence in all we do.
We pride ourselves on growing learners, leaders and citizens and equipping our children with the tools necessary to be successful in their futures.
Absence
If your child is unable to attend school it is important you notify us by the start of the school day.
Facebook
Click this link to find out what we have going on in school.
Pay Online
Please pay for your school meals, music tuition and off-site visits.
The School News
That’s a Wrap on Another Fantastic Year
Farewell Year 6 – What a Wonderful Send Off
A Fantastic Annual Sports Day
We aim to ensure that all pupils have the opportunity to develop and enhance the necessary skills, both socially and academically, to become prepared for the ever changing world ahead of them.
Every member of our school community is valued, and we work hard to ensure that everyone is happy and feels safe.
Testimonials
What our pupils, parents and carers say
My favourite aspect of King's Academy Rowner is how personal everything feels, there is such a strong sense of community. Throughout my children's time at RJS, all teaching and support staff have been extremely supportive. It is clear that the children's individual needs are at the forefront. The wide range of after school activities and broad curriculum has been exceptional. Parents are kept well informed in all aspects and any concerns have been dealt with effectively. All three of my children have attended RJS and it seems throughout the years, the school has gone from strength to strength, despite increasing pressures regarding resources and results. There are high, clear expectations and the environment is best described as nurturing and happy. It is a wonderful school with a strong learning ethos. Thank you to everyone for the past few years, for all your support and help moulding my children into resilient, independent and respectful citizens.

pageCache.pageTitle: Remote Learning Offer – King's Academy Rowner
pageCache.text:
Rowner are committed to supporting children, with home learning e.g. at weekends and in times of whole school closure or self-isolation due to medical need.
Our offer:
Minimises the disruption to pupils’ learning journey
Utilises Google Classroom for whole school closures
Educational Provision
Click here for a detailed over-view of our Remote Learning provision.
If the whole school is closed, in the first instance, pupils are to access their regular Google Classroom. This will be used to teach live lessons and provide home learning tasks. In the event we move to more than a one-day closure, the Gomer curriculum will move on-line e.g. lessons, assemblies, Google meets etc.
If a child requires a period of self-isolation due to a national pandemnic children are to access their self-isolating Google Classroom – this is different to the Google Classroom we use on a weekly basis. The classroom has been populated with a weekly timetable and subjects have been linked to teaching inputs and activities from Oak Academy. Additionally, we will include extra activities which can be used to complement the timetable or used in isolation. Access will only be given to pupils recorded as self-isolating. The self-isolating pupil will be sent an email to join the self-isolating Google Classroom or pupils can log on to their regular Google Classroom to see the invitation – just click join. Links to the self-isolating Google Classroom, accessed by the pupil log-in, can be found below. A pupil can apply to join by clicking the link:
Want to navigate around the Google Classroom? Please access our Google Quick Start Guides
Want to access the government’s online lesson platform? Oak Academy can be accessed by all learners at any time of the academic year. The Oak Academy provides teaching and learning resources for all curriculum areas and can be used for remote learning for every year group. We have aligned Oak Academy units of learning to our own curriculum to support children’s learning journeys. Please see ‘educational provision’ below. Please see video and help sheet of how to access the learning materials. No access to a device? If your child does not have access to a device such as a PC or laptop and/or the internet, it is the parents/carers responsibility to inform the school to discuss alternative arrangements.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information Report/SEND Policy/Local Offer/Gosport Directory/Accessibility – King's Academy Rowner
pageCache.text:
At Rowner, our SEND Leader (SENDCo) is Mrs Sarah Knoll. You can contact Mrs Knoll via the school office, by telephone her or by emailing her at: sknoll@kgarowner.uk
This is our SEND Report outlining the provision we are to offer in our school:
Please see our SEND Policy
Many families are not always aware of the wide range of support, advice and services available beyond school. The Hampshire Local Offer is an excellent place to start for parents and carers who may be seeking additional guidance, support or information for their child.
The Local Offer brings together information about services available for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) across Hampshire. This includes support with areas such as learning needs, emotional wellbeing, speech and language, neurodiversity, health services, short breaks, family support and much more.
At King’s Academy Rowner, we are always committed to supporting children and families as best we can. However, schools have limited in-house services and specialist capacity. Because of this, we strongly encourage families to explore the Hampshire Local Offer, which can help signpost parents and carers to a much broader range of professional advice, resources and external support services.
The Local Offer can be accessed here: Hampshire SEND Local Offer
We hope families find this resource helpful and reassuring. Accessing advice early and understanding what support is available can often make a real difference for children and young people.
Guidance Videos for Families
Parent – How to contribute to a request for assessment
Parent – How to contribute to an assessment
Parent – How to contribute ahead of a review meeting
Accessibility
Our school is a two-storey building with wide corridors, allowing easy movement throughout the premises. For any child or staff member who may find stairs challenging, ground-floor classrooms will be allocated as needed. We also provide a designated disabled parking space for blue badge holders, located next to a drop curb and flat surfaces for easy access.
The main reception is clearly signposted and fully wheelchair accessible, as are all external doors leading into the school. While our doors open outwards and may present some difficulty, our staff are always on hand to assist, including with the sign-in process.
Our reception desk is two-tiered to accommodate all visitors, with a dedicated space for wheelchair users. Additionally, our electronic sign-in system can be adjusted to different levels to meet individual needs.
We have an accessible unisex toilet in the centre of the school which is very close to our school reception. We have an additional accessible toilet at the far end of our school which is fitted with a lifting hoist. We can provide large print versions of documents if required. We are currently a dog-free site with the exception of Guide Dogs and puppies in arms.
Please let us know if you have any specific requirements by telephone, prior to your visit so that we can best facilitate your needs.
The security of the school site is very important. The car park gate is locked during the school day and visitors will be required to use on-road parking outside the school or if available the spaces to the front of our school gate and on our school site. We only have parking spaces for staff and some visitors with arrangement. To access the school please use the pedestrian gate which is to the left of the car park gate as you face it. There is an intercom system for you to alert us to your arrival. The whole site is kept secured by enhanced CCTV that operates 24 hours a day, everyday of the year.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE and Sports Premium – King's Academy Rowner
pageCache.text:
King’s Academy Rowner continues to allocate funds to a range of sporting activities and equipment, which provide better opportunities for all pupils to develop their Physical Education skills and enhance their opportunities throughout their time with us. It is important to the school that our pupils have opportunities to experience sports which may not ordinarily be available to them out of school.
King’s Academy Rowner was awarded the Bronze School Games Mark for 2024/25. This is recognition of our commitment to school sport and physical activity. This Government-led award, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust, celebrates schools that go above and beyond in promoting competition and participation both within school and the wider community.
For context, the UK government allocates PE and Sport Premium funding to primary schools based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6. Schools with 17 or more eligible pupils receive a base amount of £16,000, plus an additional £10 per pupil. Therefore, the total funding for King’s Academy Rowner in 2024-2025 was £18 190. We take pride in offering a rich and inclusive sporting curriculum. We champion those children with a natural sporting flair and ensure those who need extra encouragement are supported every step of the way. Our extra-curricular clubs are thriving and available to all.

pageCache.pageTitle: Anticipated Costings / Visits For School Year – King's Academy Rowner
pageCache.text:
To help families plan and budget, we have published an overview of the voluntary contributions we anticipate requesting throughout the academic year. This has been developed in response to parent and carer feedback, recognising the importance of providing as much notice as possible.
Wherever we can, we will give reasonable advance notice of educational visits and activities that require a voluntary contribution. Occasionally, exciting opportunities arise at short notice and, in these circumstances, it may not be possible to provide the usual notice period. If this happens, we will communicate with families as early as we can and invite your support where appropriate.
Residential visits involve significant planning and financial commitment. For this reason, we aim to provide approximately one year’s notice to allow families plenty of time to prepare. We are incredibly grateful to our dedicated staff, whose goodwill and commitment make these memorable experiences possible.
Please note that the estimated costs below are provided as a guide and may change due to factors outside the school’s control, such as transport, venue or provider costs. We may also add additional opportunities during the year if they enrich our curriculum and benefit our pupils.
As always, we strive to keep costs to a minimum, making use of the KA Gomer minibus wherever possible. However, coach travel has increased significantly in recent years and remains one of the largest costs associated with educational visits.
We greatly value the support of our parents and carers. Your voluntary contributions enable us to provide the rich, memorable experiences that enhance learning, broaden horizons and create lasting memories for our children.

Thank you for supporting us with providing your child with the correct uniform. We are proud of how smart the children look. At King’s Academy Rowner, we have a school uniform because we recognise that a consistent uniform approach increases children’s identity and self-esteem, impacting positively on behaviour. It also puts the children in the right frame of mind for working. Additionally, it ensures that pupils are not differentiated one from another because of the clothes they wear to school. We have given careful consideration to the uniform list ensuring that it is readily available and reasonably priced. Children are to wear their PE kit to school on their PE days – please see calendar for these.
PLEASE mark your child’s name in ALL clothing and personal belongings to help us return them if they are mislaid.
